Application stands disposed of.

3. The present petition under Section 482 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973 ('Cr.P.C.') has been filed on behalf of the petitioners seeking quashing of the case arising out of FIR bearing No.
917/2021, registered at Police Station New Usmanpur, for offences punishable under Sections 498A/406/34 of the Indian Penal Code, 1860 ('IPC') and Section 4 of the Dowry Prohibition Act,
1961.
4. Issue notice.
Learned APP accepts notice on behalf of the State.
5. Brief facts of the case are that the marriage was solemnized between

It is stated that a child was born out of the said wedlock.

sentences.text: 1 further submitted that on 30.12.2021, on the complaint of respondent no. 2, an FIR got registered at Police Station New Usmanpur and charge-sheet was filed.

It is stated that on 02.05.2024, both the parties amicably settled all the disputes and differences before Delhi Mediation Centre,
Karkardooma Courts, Delhi and it was inter- alia settled between the parties that petitioner no. 1 shall pay a sum of Rs. 9,25,000/- to the respondent no. 2 as full and final amount.
It is also stated that the petitioner no. 1 has already paid Rs. 2,00,000 to respondent no. 2 on 03.05.2024, at the time of withdrawal of DV case and execution petition.
It is also stated that on 20.05.2024, the marriage between petitioner no. 1 and respondent no. 2 had been dissolved as per Muslim law.
In view of the settlement, the present petition has been filed.
6. The parties are present before this Court in-person today, and have been identified by their counsel and Investigating Officer concerned.

7. Learned APP appearing on behalf of the State invites this Courts attention to paragraph 10,
where though it is mentioned that the rights of the minor child will not be affected, the wife will not initiate any litigation case against the respondents.
In view thereof, an additional affidavit which has been handed-over in the Court, wherein it is clearly mentioned that the rights of the minor child will not be affected.
Let the same be taken on record.
8. Today, the complainant who is present in Court states that she has received all amounts due to her and has no objection if the FIR is quashed.
9. In view of the above facts that the parties have amicably resolved their differences out of their own free will and without any coercion and also This is a digitally signed order.
The authenticity of the order can be re-verified from Delhi High Court Order Portal by scanning the QR code shown above.

The Order is downloaded from the DHC Server on 03/06/2024 at 22:51:04 the fact that the present matter is a family matter, I am of the opinion that no useful purpose will be served by continuing the proceedings, rather the same would create further acrimony between them.
Hence, it would be in the interest of justice to quash the abovementioned FIR and the proceedings pursuant thereto.
Moreover, there is no legal impediment in quashing the FIR in question.

10. Accordingly, FIR bearing No. 917/2021, registered at Police Station New Usmanpur, for offences punishable under Sections 498A/406/34 of the IPC and all consequential proceedings emanating therefrom are quashed.

11. The petition stands disposed of.
12. The order be uploaded on the website forthwith.
SWARANA KANTA SHARMA, J MAY 30, 2024/at
